For a language whose frozen recipe has no separate build step, this metric is N/A for that language with reason 'language_has_no_separate_build_step_in_its_frozen_recipe', excluded from the applicable-weight denominator for that language only, and the remaining weights renormalised per spec 26. That is a genuine inapplicability of the quantity, not a missing capability being hidden: the language's startup and parse cost is still fully visible in Generated Code Performance, which measures the whole run. Same no-passing-version rule (score 0 with reason) for languages that do have a build step.

presentation_row_mapping._authority: spec 9.1, fixed so that two runs do not invent different correspondences.

metric_definitions_and_weights.presentation_is_presentation_only: The twelve-row table of spec 28.2 is presentation only. It displays twelve of the eighteen weighted metrics. The six listed above still carry their weights and still enter the LLM Practical Effectiveness Score. The full eighteen-metric breakdown is preserved in results/llm_practical_full_breakdown.{json,md} and the score is computed from the eighteen, never from the twelve.
metric_definitions_and_weights.score_formula: LLM Practical Effectiveness Score(L) = sum over applicable metrics m of ( weight_m * Score_m(L) ) / sum over applicable metrics m of weight_m. Scores clipped to [0, 100], reported to two decimal places, ranked on unrounded values (spec 25.3).
metric_definitions_and_weights.ranking: An independent LLM Practical Effectiveness Ranking is produced from this score alone. It is never merged with Intrinsic Learnability, Semantic Compression, or Standard, and no cross-evaluation overall score or overall ranking is created (spec 28.2, spec 32).

na_policy_for_llm_practical.rule: N/A is never silently converted to zero and never used to let a missing capability escape scoring. A genuinely inapplicable metric is excluded from that language's applicable-weight denominator and the remaining weights are renormalised.

the_only_permitted_na_reasons.scope: all ten languages simultaneously or none
the_only_permitted_na_reasons.justification: The quantity is not observable through this client. It is not a property of any language.
There is no build command to time. The cost is not hidden: it is inside Generated Code Performance, which times the whole run.
There was nothing to repair. Repair Efficiency still scores 100 for such a language by family E, so the language is not credited twice.

the_only_permitted_na_reasons.metric: any metric whose cells all failed after 3 retries
the_only_permitted_na_reasons.justification: Spec 6.2 forbids converting provider/infrastructure failure into a language or model failure. The shortfall is published in _deviations.json and in the results summary.

explicitly_not_na: A language that produced no passing program scores 0 on Generated Code Performance, Generated Code Memory Efficiency, Generated Code Compile Performance (if it has a build step) and Source Token Efficiency, with the reason recorded. It is not N/A.
A language the model handles badly is scored badly, not marked N/A.
A capability a language lacks that a task requires produces a failing class for that task, not N/A.
na_policy_for_llm_practical.every_na_documented: Every N/A written anywhere in the LLM Practical results carries its reason_code, the affected language, the affected metric, the renormalised applicable-weight denominator, and the resulting score both with and without the exclusion, so the effect of the exclusion is visible.

source_token_counting._purpose: Source Token Efficiency needs one counter applied identically to ten languages.
source_token_counting.governing_implementation: scripts/tokenize_source.py. If a benchmark-wide source tokenizer already exists for the Semantic Compression track, that implementation governs both tracks and this section states the behaviour it must have. Either way exactly one implementation is used for all ten languages and its SHA-256 is recorded in the results.
source_token_counting.rule: Read the source file as UTF-8. Remove comments using the language's comment syntax as listed in tokenize_source.py's fixed per-language comment table (line-comment prefix and block-comment delimiters only; no other language knowledge is used). Then emit tokens by scanning left to right and matching, in this order: (1) a string or character literal including its delimiters, counted as ONE token regardless of length; (2) a numeric literal; (3) an identifier or keyword, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* plus any non-ASCII letter; (4) a maximal run of operator or punctuation characters that the language's fixed operator table lists as a single operator, otherwise a single character. Whitespace and newlines are not tokens.
source_token_counting.why_a_lexical_counter_and_not_the_model_: The model's own tokenizer is not exposed by this client for arbitrary strings, and a BPE count would make Source Token Efficiency partly a measure of how the tokenizer happens to segment each language's identifiers. The lexical counter measures source structure, is reproducible by a third party with no provider access, and is applied identically to all ten. Where the harness does report input-token counts for packs, those are published beside the lexical counts and never substituted for them.
source_token_counting.comment_handling_disclosure: Comments are removed before counting, for all ten languages identically. This means a language whose generated code carries more explanatory comments is not penalised, and one that carries fewer is not rewarded. The comment-inclusive count is also published as a raw figure.

trial_preservation_layout._authority: spec 23 (complete preservation of LLM trials) and spec 24 (prompt preservation).
trial_preservation_layout.reconstruction_guarantee: From this layout alone, with no access to this conversation and no access to the model, a third party can reconstruct prompt -> generated program -> failure -> diagnosis -> repair -> final result for every trial, including every version that contained a Silent Bug.
trial_preservation_layout.path_grammar: <root>/<task_id>/<language_slug>/trial_<NN>/ where NN is the trial index zero-padded to two digits, 01-based. task_id is one of the frozen ids in trial_allocation. language_slug is one of quidra, python, cpp, rust, go, java, typescript, kotlin, swift, zig. Nothing else appears at those levels.
directory_tree: <root>/_aborted/<task_id>__<language_slug>__trial_<NN>__attempt_<A>/   (preserved partial directory of any attempt discarded for an infrastructure event)
trial_preservation_layout.version_directories_are_created_only_whe: repair_02/ exists only if repair turn 2 was issued. Its absence means the trial ended earlier and is not a gap in the record; manifest.json states repair_turns_used explicitly.

manifest.json.note: 'scored' is false for the DIAG-NOPACK trials and for any invalidated trial; 'excluded_reason' says why.

file_semantics.prompts/system_prompt.txt: The fully substituted system prompt, byte-exact as delivered.
file_semantics.prompts/user_prompt_initial.txt: The fully substituted task prompt, byte-exact as delivered, including the task specification text and the on-disk pointers to the pack.
file_semantics.prompts/pack_manifest.json: Relative path, byte size, and SHA-256 of every file under prompts/pack/, plus the pack token counts by the frozen counter.
file_semantics.prompts/pack/: A verbatim copy of every file the trial could read as reference material. Spec 24 requires supplied language specifications and examples to be preserved; keeping them inside the trial, rather than only by reference, means a third party needs nothing else.
file_semantics.prompts/repair_prompt_NN.txt: The fully substituted repair prompt, byte-exact as delivered, including the real truncated diagnostics.
file_semantics.prompts/final_input_reconstruction.json: An ordered list of every message delivered to the model in this trial, each as {role, source_file, sha256}, so the exact final input presented to the model can be reconstructed byte for byte (spec 24).
file_semantics.versions/<id>/model_output.md: The subagent's raw returned text for that turn, verbatim, before any extraction.
file_semantics.versions/<id>/source/<ENTRY_FILENAME>: The source file exactly as it stood on disk when the turn ended. Read-only (0444). This is the artefact that is built and scored.
file_semantics.versions/<id>/oracle_diff.txt: Expected vs actual for every failing check, verbatim and untruncated. The truncated form is what went into the repair prompt; this is the full record.

versions/<id>/classification.json.note: silent_bug_conditions records the five boolean conditions (a)-(e) individually, so the classification can be re-derived by hand.

file_semantics.versions/<id>/sha256sums.txt: SHA-256, byte size, and mtime in nanoseconds of every file under source/, captured before any build step. Re-verified at scoring; a mismatch invalidates the trial.

diagnosis/diagnosis_NN.json.note: 'improved' and 'misdiagnosis' are computed by the mechanical improvement ladder. source_diff_unified is a unified diff from the previous version's source to this one, so the repair itself is visible.

tokens/usage.json.note: per_turn carries {version_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens, wall_clock_ns}. Any field the harness does not report is null, never estimated. 'source_of_numbers' records exactly which harness field each number came from, or 'unavailable'.

file_semantics.logs/agent_tool_calls.jsonl: One JSON object per tool call the subagent made: timestamp_utc, tool, arguments_summary, allowed_or_denied, duration_ns. This is the audit trail for the no-retrieval and no-human-edit enforcement.
file_semantics.logs/timeline.jsonl: Ordered events: trial_start, prompt_delivered, turn_end, build_start/end, run_start/end, oracle_start/end, repair_issued, trial_end, each with timestamp_utc.
file_semantics.logs/errors.txt: Any orchestrator-side error text for this trial, verbatim. Infrastructure events also appear in the run-level _infrastructure_events.jsonl.

final/result.json.note: measured_* are present only when the final version is PASS, because performance is measured on passing programs only; otherwise null with the reason 'no_passing_generated_program'.

file_semantics.final/source/<ENTRY_FILENAME>: A read-only copy of the final version's source, so the end state is reachable without walking the version chain.

index_files._index.json: One row per trial with: task_id, language, trial_index, schedule_index, scored, final_classification, repair_turns_used, correct_at_1, path. Plus a header block with per-cell trials_planned, trials_executed, trials_scored. This is the file the reporting obligation on executed counts is computed from.
index_files._execution_order.json: The frozen schedule: the enumerated triples, their LCG sort keys, the deterministic spread-constraint repair steps, and the final ordered list. Written before the first trial.
index_files._infrastructure_events.jsonl: Every provider, rate-limit, transport, timeout, context-exhaustion, harness, host, and model-identity event, with the action taken. Separate from all language and model failures, per spec 6.2.
index_files._deviations.json: Every departure from this frozen configuration, with class, affected cells, reason, date, and effect on the metrics. Classes: source_mutated_after_capture, retrieval_violation, infrastructure_exhausted, trial_count_shortfall, signature_list_amendment, other. An empty list is written if there are none, so the absence of deviations is itself recorded rather than inferred.

trial_preservation_layout.immutability: Trial directories are written once and then made read-only. Re-running a cell writes a new attempt directory; it never overwrites a preserved one. Nothing under trials/ is deleted, including aborted attempts, failed generations, and silent-bug versions (spec 32 forbids hiding failed trials and inconvenient raw data).
trial_preservation_layout.prompt_preservation_cross_reference: Spec 24 additionally requires preservation of adversarial-test prompts, unseen-case prompts, and prompt-robustness variations. The unseen-case and robustness prompts live in these trial directories by construction (UG-G1-unseen and PR-R1-v1..v3 are task_ids). The authored source of every task specification and every prompt variation, before substitution, is preserved at llm-practical/tasks/<task_id>/ with SHA-256, and the adversarial-test prompts belong to the adversarial suite's own directory.

reporting_obligations._authority: spec 6.2 allocation paragraph, spec 25.1 family-C disclosure, spec 26, spec 32.

O2. Attach the frozen precision sentence to every table row backed by fewer than five trials per language, stating the actual N.
O3. Never describe a few-point difference between languages in a one-trial row as a resolved difference, and never attach a ranking, interval, or significance claim to it.
O4. Publish, for the five-trial cells, the per-trial outcomes and the statement that a five-trial rate resolves to 20 percentage points.
O5. Publish the duplication rate per cell where deterministic decoding produced byte-identical trials.
O6. Publish infrastructure events per language and state that none of them entered any metric.

O7. For every family-C metric whose applicable raw values span a factor of 100 or more, publish the raw value in its natural unit for every language, the ratio to the best value, and the compression note required by spec 25.1.
O8. Publish every N/A with its reason_code, its effect on the applicable-weight denominator, and the score with and without the exclusion.
O9. Publish the full eighteen-metric weighted breakdown alongside the twelve-row presentation table, and state that the score comes from the eighteen.
O10. Publish the silent-bug list, the hallucination-match list, and the detection-coverage asymmetry disclosure.
O11. Publish the statement that no generated source was edited by a human, with the count of trials whose source hashes verified.
O12. Publish the DIAG-NOPACK results in their own table, labelled a diagnostic of prior knowledge, with an explicit statement that they contribute to no score (spec 9).
O13. Publish _deviations.json contents in the results summary, including the case where it is empty.
reporting_obligations.frozen_precision_sentence: This row is measured with N trial(s) per language. Differences of a few points between languages are not resolved by this measurement and must not be read as a ranking.

amendment_and_freeze_rules.frozen_at: 2026-09-17, before the first scored LLM generation of run 2026-09-17-7677581.

altering a task, an oracle, or a compliance checklist
adding or removing a prompt variation
